precedent_checks.work: Methodological precedents named in the brief: Elek-Szabo 2004 (sofic => stably finite); Gardam 2021 unit counterexample (arXiv:2102.11818, Ann. Math. 194); Dykema-Heister-Juschenko 2015 (ULIE groups); Gardam's ERC project SATURN (CORDIS 101076148, 2023-10-01 to 2028-09-30)

comparison.detail: Analyst derivation: a sofic N would give a Sylvester rank function with rk(P_v) = 1/kappa, so UT = I_m forces m <= t/kappa, i.e. t >= m*kappa. CT's data has t <= m(D^2/2 - 1) < m*kappa. The criterion is therefore exactly a certificate that beats the sofic rank bound, and it can exist only because sum_f sum_{v in f} W_v = D * sum_V W_v forces D = 0 in K. This also implies the glued group N itself must be nonsofic if CT is correct.

Gardam fixes a group (the Promislow/Hantzsche-Wendt group P) and finds a nontrivial unit in F2[P] by SAT search (domain knowledge; the abstract only says 'the group is virtually abelian and the field is order two'). SATURN aims at a DF counterexample by SAT and says it 'will give the first example of a non-sofic group'. 197 does no search: it designs the group around a finite certificate (CT) or around a parity count (TF), then proves the group is nondegenerate. Gardam is a precedent for 'F2 counterexamples to a Kaplansky conjecture exist', not for any 197 item.

comparison.verdict: nearest group-theoretic precedent for 'design the group around the cancellation'
comparison.detail: DHJ build the universal finitely presented group from the cancellation pattern of ab = 1 at fixed support sizes and verify small cases by computer. CT's N is built from incidence data, not from a support pattern. TF's cone group is built from immersed graphs. Both are genuinely different from ULIE presentations.

precedent_checks.verdict: No AI provenance. Gardam is a methodological precedent only.

candidates.name: Incidence criterion
paper_items: sec. 'From subgroup averages to the scalar defect' (02-criterion.tex)
candidates.statement: Let ell be an odd prime, K a finite field of characteristic 2 containing a primitive ell-th root of unity, kappa = ell^2. Given an (ell+1)-regular finite set system (V,F) of incidence girth >= 12 and x_v in K^m with sum_V x_v x_v^T = -I_m, sum_{v in f} x_v x_v^T = 0 for every f, and 0 < m < |V| <= m*kappa, there are a finitely presented G with ell-torsion and a,b in K[G] with ab = 1 != ba.

final.justification: The only item in the family with no neighbour found in any field and no retrieval trigger in the trace. Its content is a finite certificate that beats the sofic rank bound (t < m*kappa) by exploiting D = ell+1 = 0 in K. That is exactly why it cannot exist in characteristic 0 and why it forces nonsoficity. Against: every component is standard (averaging idempotents, glued finite groups, HNN character twists, augmentation specialization, DJ transfer). It emerged incrementally from the model's own early CEX lessons at pivot distance 1. Like 287's C2, the eureka content lies in posing the right finite data, and the proof after that is routine. common.models: Training-data cutoff strictly before 2026-07-31, when OpenAI's 'Nonsofic Groups Exist' first circulated. This is earlier than every 197 manuscript and ZD (2026-09-23). Canary probe: exclude any model that (i) states that a nonsofic group is known, (ii) knows of any claimed counterexample to Kaplansky's DF or zero-divisor conjectures, or (iii) recognises 'incidence criterion', 'punctured affine space' or 'parity criterion' in this context. No browsing, retrieval or tools. Exclude the OpenAI 'Astra' / GPT-5.6 Sol lineage that produced the release and the August result; run it only as an uncontrolled reference arm. Note Thom's (disputed) allegation that this lineage saw private ChatGPT conversations on expanders/soficity. The judge must be a different model from the proposer.
common.context_L_minus: CT arms: Mathlib d13f23b digest (MonoidAlgebra, Matrix, FiniteField, MvPolynomial, PresentedGroup) plus CT's bibliography MINUS DeterminantCompanion and UniversalFinftyCompanion (19 entries), each as abstract plus invoked statements. Sub-arm L--: also remove GolowichLin2024 and DinurLiuZhang2025 to measure the retrieval effect seen in the trace (PV4). TF arms: TF's bibliography MINUS OpenAI2026ZD and OpenAI2026DF (11 entries). L(TF) arm adds ZD to measure precedent uplift.

arms.L: adds the model-produced companions (ZD for TF; CT for DT/OD)
arms.open: problem statement only ('Is K[G] directly finite for every field K and group G?'); tests the PROVE/CEX decision too

common.sampling: n = 256 independent samples per arm, temperature 1.0, fixed reasoning budget (e.g. 32k tokens). Unbiased pass@k for k in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256}; K = 256.
common.judging: Two independent LLM judges, given the paper's own precedent remarks (CT 01-introduction 'The construction', 03-pairing.tex:17-24; TF introduction.tex:50-54, 82-85) and this file's neighbour lists. A human group-ring expert checks all hits and 10% of misses. Lean equivalence where a Lean statement exists (CT: AlgebraicCriterion.square_witnesses, PolynomialPairing.sum_complement_gram; DT: GroupRingDeterminant.*; OD: OddKaplansky.*). Hits are 'equivalent up to normalisation'.
common.controls: Positive: Cook-Reckhow ER extension variables for PHP. Negative: C7 (DJ matrix units), C9 (CA transfer), C6 (planar Euler embedding) in the same format.
common.prompt_template: Problem: [open or directed statement]. Library: [L- digest]. Established results you may use: [non-hidden upstream items, verbatim]. Propose the single most useful new lemma, definition or construction, stated precisely, with a proof sketch.

P-C1.item: C1 incidence criterion (with C2 and C5 as sub-criteria)
P-C1.hide: thm:criterion and everything downstream: sec. 'From subgroup averages to the scalar defect', prop:pairing (C3), thm:hypergraph (C4), lem:embedding (C6), sec. 5 prescription, sec. 6 CA
P-C1.arm_A_pivot: Give DJ, Elek-Szabo, averaging idempotents of finite subgroups, and the hint that a one-sided inverse must violate every Sylvester rank function. Expected moderate hit rate.
P-C1.arm_B_decisive: Open problem plus L- only, with no rank-function hint and no CEX direction. This is the analogue of the trace's restart-free setting.
P-C1.equivalence: Hit = a finite combinatorial-linear certificate that, via glued finite subgroups (or any finite-subgroup idempotents), yields a rectangular identity UT = I_m through t intermediate coordinates with t < m * (inverse rank of the idempotents), using a characteristic-dependent local cancellation. Sub-criteria: (a) the subgroup-average Gram identity (C2); (b) packing plus specialization certificate (C5). Partial credit is recorded for (a) alone.
P-C1.pivot_distance: 1 (trace: from K11/K12/K19; dormant clause K11 from 0.15 to 0.425)

P-C3.hide: prop:pairing, lem:interpolation, lem:line-sums and downstream (thm:hypergraph, sec. 5)
P-C3.arms: L- vs L-- (without GL/DLZ). The trace says the retrieval of GL/DLZ triggered it, so the L-- vs L- gap measures transfer dependence.
P-C3.equivalence: Any explicit family x_v in K^m on a finite point set with rank-one Gram sums vanishing on every block of a regular high-girth set system and total -I_m, with m < t <= m*ell^2. Polynomial or not, characteristic 2 required.

P-T1.item: T1 parity criterion for ab = 1 (with T2 as sub-criterion)
P-T1.arms: L(TF) with ZD vs L-(TF) without ZD. With ZD the hit rate is expected to be near-certain (adaptation). Without ZD, T1 is really testing ZD's parity mechanism (family 196).
P-T1.equivalence: Elements a = sum g_x, b = sum g_x^{-1} (or equivalent) over cone/graphical groups with a simultaneous-step parity count in which exactly one component, the root's, has odd size.

P-D1.item: D1 DF failure in char 2 => Determinant Conjecture failure
P-D1.hide: all of DT after Theorem 1.1 input (prop:separation, lem:lift, shear analysis)
P-D1.give: CT Theorem 1.1 as a black box; Luck 2002; FK 1952; Dicks-Schick
P-D1.equivalence: Any construction of an integral matrix over Z[G'] (G' built from H2) invertible over Q[G'] with 0 < det_FK < 1 from a2*b2 = 1 != b2*a2, or a proof of that implication.
P-D1.pivot_distance: 1 (trace L101-105: model proposed the lamp-projection amplification at share ~0.05)

P-O1.item: O1 triangular compression from low-rank fits
P-O1.arms: with vs without CT in L (sibling architecture)
P-O1.equivalence: A one-sided inverse obtained from a graph (or set system) with a low-rank fitting matrix plus idempotents whose rank fraction exceeds t/m, via ordered or orthogonal annihilations.
